plan.title: Liver treated vs control: DESeq2 DE + Hallmark/Reactome GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: Raw STAR/featureCounts gene-level counts for 6 human liver samples (3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch) are analyzed with the DESeq2 pipeline grounded by the knowledge service (snapshot sha256:ad61b0ba14...). Step 1 runs sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA on top-500-variance genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) to confirm the treated/control samples separate and no sample is an outlier before any test is fit. Step 2 builds the DESeq2 dataset directly from the integer count matrix (no length correction, no tximport, per R-0064 since the counts are STAR+featureCounts gene-level), applies a minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=3 samples, the smallest group size), sets the explicit reference level (control) on the condition factor, and runs the Wald test; apeglm shrinks the treated-vs-control log2 fold change. edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test runs on the same filtered counts and design as a second method; the report gives the intersection of the two significant-gene sets as the high-confidence call and each method's unique calls as secondary, per R-0042. Because n=3/group, the plan explicitly states the expected power limitation (R-0017/R-0094): the DE list is not exhaustive and only large effects are reliably detected. Step 3 does BH-adjusted multiple testing (alpha=0.05, independent filtering on, p-value histogram inspected before trusting the adjustment) and selects genes by adjusted p-value only. Step 4 runs fgsea preranked GSEA (ranked on the DESeq2 Wald statistic, per the disputed-metric rule resolved in favor of 'stat') against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) and Reactome (follow-up), both confirmed present in the reference store for human, with the standard 15-500 gene set size window and redundancy collapsing. Step 5 assembles the final report: DE method, package versions, design formula and named contrast (condition: treated vs control), thresholds, n tested vs n DE, MA/dispersion diagnostic plots, DESeq2-vs-edgeR overlap, leading-edge genes per significant pathway, the small-n power caveat, and a full reproducibility record (sessionInfo, seed, package and gene-set-collection versions).
